stem: In item analysis, the proportion of students who answered a given test item correctly is called its:
explanation: The difficulty index (p-value) is simply the fraction of test-takers who got an item right — a high value means an easy item, a low value a hard one — distinct from the discrimination index, which measures how well an item distinguishes high scorers from low scorers.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: In item analysis, the measure showing how well a test item distinguishes between high-performing students (who tend to get it right) and low-performing students (who tend to get it wrong) is called its:
explanation: A good test item should have a positive discrimination index — high scorers answer it correctly more often than low scorers — items with a poor or negative discrimination index (low scorers doing better) are typically flagged and revised or discarded.

stem: Before setting a question paper, a teacher prepares a two-way grid mapping content topics against cognitive levels (knowledge, understanding, application, etc.), assigning the number/weightage of questions to each cell, to ensure the paper covers the syllabus proportionately. This planning document is called a:
explanation: The Table of Specification (or test blueprint) ensures balanced content and cognitive-level coverage before item-writing begins — distinct from a marking scheme (guidance for awarding marks after the paper is set) or a question bank (a large pool of ready-made items).
